- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and supply net is large negative, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward drag or lagged mean reversion to prevent overextension.
- In high-event periods (e.g., >15 events/30d, net supply negative), model underestimates downside risk — increase downward bias or add volatility penalty to forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and supply is negative, model often fails to anticipate sharp drops — add early warning buffer or adjust for “bearish sentiment lag”.
- In low-event periods (e.g., <10 events), model tends to overestimate stability — reduce forecast variance or apply mean reversion toward recent 7–14 day average.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes followed by recovery, model often misses the “rebound lag” — adjust forecast to allow 2–3 day delay in reversal.
- For CAP3 EU auctions with high supply net, model often ignores policy impact — reduce forecast by 2–5% for each CAP3 EU auction within 7 days.
- When bullish sentiment is low but supply is negative, model often overestimates upside — apply downward bias of 1–3% to offset sentiment misalignment.
